name: Arize
tagline: MCP-Native Eval vs Enterprise ML Observability
oneLine: The agent observability and evaluation platform: Phoenix (open-source observability and evals) plus Arize AX (managed AI engineering platform).
tldrVendor: Arize describes itself as 'the agent observability and evaluation platform': Phoenix (open-source observability and evals, Elastic License 2.0) for self-hosted tracing, evaluation, experimentation and prompt iteration, plus Arize AX (managed AI engineering platform) with online evals, dashboards, the Alyx agent, SOC 2 Type II, SSO and RBAC. Embedding drift monitoring lives in its ML observability product. In August 2026 Arize announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Dynatrace.

rows.quote: built on top of OpenTelemetry and is vendor, language, and framework agnostic

rows.vendor: Phoenix: pip install arize-phoenix; SQLite by default, PostgreSQL supported; Docker, Kubernetes/Helm options
rows.quote: If URL is not specified, by default Phoenix starts with a file-based SQLite database in a temporary folder.

rows.vendor: OpenTelemetry SDK + OpenInference auto-instrumentation in the app, exporting to the Phoenix collector endpoint
rows.quote: the OpenInference CrewAI auto-instrumentation package, which handles tracing for us without requiring manual instrumentation.

rows.vendor: LLM-as-a-Judge, agent-as-a-judge or code evaluators (AX); Phoenix response and retrieval evals
rows.quote: Evaluate agent performance with LLM-as-a-Judge, agent-as-a-judge, or code evaluators.

rows.vendor: Token and cost tracking across models
rows.quote: The costs are calculated from token counts and model pricing data, then rolled up to the trace and project level for comprehensive cost analysis.

rows.vendor: Phoenix MCP server (prompts, traces, datasets, experiments, SQL); no tool runs an eval
rows.quote: Phoenix MCP Server is an implementation of the Model Context Protocol for the Arize Phoenix platform. It provides a unified interface to Phoenix's capabilities.

rows.quote: Today we are announcing the signing of a definitive agreement for the acquisition of Arize by Dynatrace to accelerate that proposition.

rows.vendor: AX dashboards from templates or blank, widget-based; Alyx AI engineering agent; Prompt Playground
rows.quote: Two ways to get started: pick a pre-configured template or start with a blank dashboard.

rows.vendor: 40+ models, frameworks and AI tools; 21 Python tracing integrations in Phoenix (OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, DSPy…)
rows.quote: Arize integrates with 40+ models, frameworks, and AI tools

rows.vendor: Prompt Playground + Prompt Hub versioning; optimization manually, via Alyx, or automated Prompt Learning
rows.quote: Every iteration is committed back to the Prompt Hub as a new version, so the optimization history is auditable and the winner is deployable like any other version.

rows.vendor: SOC 2 Type II (Pro/Enterprise); Enterprise SSO, org and space RBAC, self-hosted deployment; online evals on all tiers

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Arize?
faq.vendorPart: Arize calls itself 'the agent observability and evaluation platform': Phoenix (open-source observability and evals, Elastic License 2.0) for self-hosting, and Arize AX (managed AI engineering platform) in the cloud. In August 2026 Arize announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Dynatrace.

faq.question: Is Iris better than Arize for MCP agent evaluation?
faq.vendorPart: Arize requires OpenTelemetry instrumentation (Phoenix is built on top of OpenTelemetry with OpenInference auto-instrumentation) but offers embedding drift monitoring for ML models, LLM-as-a-Judge, agent-as-a-judge and code evaluators, and enterprise features such as SSO and RBAC.
